name: Question 3
problem:
$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}x+1, & x\in [-2,0) \\ -2, & x\in [0,2)\end{aligned}
$$

The above function $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [-2,2).$ Let $f(x)$ be the $4$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R.$
Select the correct options below.

| I. | $F(x)$ is continuous on $x\in (-2,2)$ | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| II. | $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-2,2)$ | {{field-2}} |
| III. | ${lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}F(x)$ | {{field-3}} |
| IV. | $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth and continuous on $R$ | {{field-4}} |
worked_solution:
Let's examine the given statements in turn.

- Statement I is $\text{false}.$ The function $F(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x=0.$ Its graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069003/assets/7cfd6da222fb36d06be1153ac0e398e567f8b9fb8cd1cd9e21f1bb35ed131f8d.png)

- Statement II is $\text{true}.$ The function $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-2,2).$ It consists of two smooth pieces.

- Statement III is $\text{false}.$ Indeed, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}(x+1)=-2+1=-1
$$

and 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}(-2)=-2.
$$

So, ${lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}F(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}F(x).$

- Statement IV is $\text{false}$ since statements I and III are false.

**Note:** The $4$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R$ has the graph shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069003/assets/a59fad69c9790a2b899c21fd730f779c28bc9b70f44a67851ad5ca92bff21951.png)
